cues.en: Very possible, Lizzie. Very possible.
cues.zh: 很有可能，莉齐。很有可能。

cues.en: Alright. Who would have thought thirty years ago,
cues.zh: 好吧。三十年前谁能想到，

cues.en: we'd all be sitting here drinking Chateau de Chassele, aide.
cues.zh: 我们会坐在这儿喝着香特·德·沙塞勒酒，助手。

cues.en: Them days, we're glad to have the price of a cup of tea. Alright. A cup of cold tea. What? Without milk or sugar or tea.
cues.zh: 那时候，我们能买得起一杯茶就谢天谢地了。好吧，一杯凉茶。什么？没奶，没糖，也没茶。

cues.en: In a cracked cup and all. Oh, we never used to have a cup.
cues.zh: 杯子还裂了。哦，我们以前连杯子都没有。

cues.en: We used to have to drink out of a roll up newspaper.
cues.zh: 我们只能用卷起来的报纸喝水。

cues.en: The best we could manage was to suck on a piece of damp cloth. But, you know, we were happy in those days, although we were poor. Because we were poor. Aye. My old dad used to say to me, money doesn't bring you happiness, son. He was right. Aye. I was happier then, and I had nothing.
cues.zh: 我们能做到的最好，也就是吸一块湿布。不过，那时候我们很快乐，虽然很穷。因为我们穷。是啊，我老爸常对我说：“儿子，钱不会带来幸福。”他说得没错。是啊，那时候我更快乐，一无所有。

cues.en: We used to live in this tiny old tumbledown house with great big holes in the roof. House? Were You lucky to live in a house. We used to live in one room, all 26 of us, no furniture, half the floor was missing. We're all huddled together in one corner for fear of falling. You
cues.zh: 我们以前住在一间破旧狭小、屋顶到处是大洞的房子里。房子？能有房子住算你们走运。我们以前26个人挤在一个房间里，一件家具都没有，地板还塌了一半。我们全缩在一个角落里，生怕掉下去。你们

cues.en: were lucky to have a room. We used to have to live in the corridor.
cues.zh: 能有个房间算走运了。我们以前只能住在走廊里。

cues.en: Oh, we used to dream of living in a corridor.
cues.zh: 噢，住在走廊里那曾是我们的梦想。

cues.en: Would have been a palace to us.
cues.zh: 对我们来说那简直就是宫殿了。

cues.en: We used to live in an old water tank on a rubbish tip.
cues.zh: 我们以前住在垃圾场的一个旧水箱里。

cues.en: We got woke up every morning by having a load of rotting fish dumped all over us.
cues.zh: 每天早上，一堆腐烂的鱼倒在我们身上，把我们弄醒。

cues.en: House. Well,
cues.zh: 房子。好吧，

cues.en: when I say house, it was just a hole in the ground covered by a sheet of tarpaulin,
cues.zh: 我说房子，其实只是地上一个洞，上面盖着一块防水布，

cues.en: but it was a house to us.
cues.zh: 但对我们来说，那就是家。

cues.en: We were evicted from our hole in the ground.
cues.zh: 我们被从地洞里赶了出来。

cues.en: We had to go and live in a lake.
cues.zh: 我们只好去住在湖里。

cues.en: You were lucky to have a lake. There were a 150 of us living in a shoebox in the middle of the road.
cues.zh: 有湖住你就偷着乐吧。我们一百五十口人挤在马路中间的一个鞋盒里。

cues.en: Cardboard box. Aye. You were lucky.
cues.zh: 纸箱。没错。你们真走运。

cues.en: We lived for three months in a rolled up newspaper in a septic tank.
cues.zh: 我们曾经在化粪池里，裹着一张卷起来的报纸，住了三个月。

cues.en: You just have to get up every morning at 06:00 and clean the newspaper, go to work down the mill, fourteen hours a day, week in, week out for six months a week. And when we got home, our dad would thrash us to sleep with his belt.
cues.zh: 我们每天早上六点就得起床，把报纸清理干净，再去磨坊上班。一天十四个小时，周而复始，整整六个月。回到家后，爸爸还会用皮带把我们抽到睡着。

cues.en: Luxury.
cues.zh: 真奢侈。

cues.en: We used to have to get out of the lake at 03:00 in the morning, clean the lake, eat a handful of hot gravel, work twenty hours a day at mill for tuppence a month, come home, and dad would beat us around the head and neck with a broken bottle if we were lucky.
cues.zh: 我们以前凌晨三点就得从湖里爬出来，把湖清理干净，抓一把烫手的碎石子吃，然后去磨坊干活，每天二十个小时，一个月只挣两便士。回家后，爸爸还会拿碎酒瓶打我们的头和脖子——要是我们走运的话。

cues.en: Well, of course, we had it tough.
cues.zh: 哎，当然了，我们当年日子可苦了。

cues.en: We used to have to get him out of the shoebox in the middle of the night and lick the road clean with our toes.
cues.zh: 我们过去大半夜就得从鞋盒里爬出来，用脚趾头把马路舔干净。

cues.en: We had to eat our behind him for the freezing cold gravel, work twenty four hours of that mill for four months every six years. And when we got home, our dad would slash into it with a bread knife.
cues.zh: 我们得啃着冰冷的碎石度日，在那个作坊里每六年连轴干四个月、每天24小时不休。等回到家，我爸还会拿切面包的刀往我们身上砍。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 可不是嘛。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: had to get up in the morning at 10:00 at night, half an hour before I went to bed,
cues.zh: 早晨起床得赶在晚上10点，比我睡觉的时间还早半个小时，

cues.en: eat a lump of coal poison, work 29 a day down mill, and pay mill owner for permission to come to work. And when we got home, our dad would kill us and dance about in our grave singing hallelujah.
cues.zh: 吞下一块带毒的煤块，每天在磨坊干29个小时，还得倒贴钱给工场主才让来上班。等回到家，我爸会把我们打死，还在我们坟头上一边跳舞一边唱哈利路亚。

cues.en: Are you trying to tell the young people of today that?
cues.zh: 你是想跟今天的年轻人这么说吗？

cues.en: And they won't believe you. No. They won't.
cues.zh: 他们不会信你的。不会的。他们不会信的。
